title: [C18T1] - Percentage of the population living in cities
prompt: The graph below shows information about the percentage of the population in four Asian countries living in cities from 1970 to 2020, with predictions for 2030 and 2040. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph illustrates the proportion of people living in cities in four Asian nations from 1970 to 2020, with projections until 2040.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the urban population increased in all four countries during the period, with Malaysia showing the most substantial rise. In addition, Malaysia maintained the highest percentage among the four countries throughout most of the period, while Thailand recorded the lowest figures.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the countries with the most significant changes, Malaysia and Indonesia started at around 30% and 15% respectively in 1970. Thereafter, Malaysia's urban population rose dramatically to roughly 75% in 2020, before projections indicate a further increase to about 82% by 2040. Similarly, Indonesia's figures climbed steadily to about 50% in 2020, and forecasts suggest they will reach approximately 60% by the end of the period.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the remaining countries, Philippines and Thailand began at different levels, with the respective figures of 32% and 18% in 1970. The Philippines' percentage rose to 48% by 1990, but then declined slightly to about 44% by 2020, with predictions showing a slight rise to 51% by 2040. Meanwhile, Thailand saw the most gradual growth to 32% by 2020, though projections suggest an acceleration to about 47% by 2040.
